runtime: Bun 1.4.3; native Alchemy workerd, R2 and Queue; local shared Linux host
contract: The installed bun test --help declares --parallel=N as file-level worker processes with isolation enabled by default. --concurrent is not used; order inside files stays unchanged. CI already pins Bun 1.4.3.

change.check: Build, SDK generation, typecheck, Clippy and Cargo remain ordered before bun run test. The test script owns the concurrency argument.
change.bounds: Two worker processes instead of the machine CPU count; all per-suite runtime, R2 persistence and Queue scopes are retained. No new runner, mocked services, removed tests or relaxed timeouts.

limits: Observed local wall times, not a controlled CI or memory benchmark. Host is shared. Between runs the final SDK consumer fixture gained readonly mutation rejection and was rebuilt and verified by four focused SDK tests and exact archive binding proof. The application behavior and test count remain the same; assertion counts can vary with asynchronous observation. Production latency/cost is unrelated to this test scheduling change.

delivery.ci: Not remotely verified; GitHub work remains deferred at user request.
delivery.readonly: See shell-readonly.json for runtime and deployment evidence.

followUpCI.failure: The binary-shell aggregate test hit the implicit native Bun 5000 ms host observation deadline. All other tests, including readonly and metadata repair, passed.
followUpCI.correction: Only the aggregate binary-shell integration test gets an explicit 15000 ms observation budget. It retains all 79 assertions, real R2/WASI execution and scope cleanup. Worker execution limits, fixture sizes, test concurrency and the other test deadlines remain unchanged.
followUpCI.limits: The normal native test runtime is unchanged; this is host scheduling allowance for a multi-operation integration test, not evidence of lower execution latency. A warm Rust cache restored the installed wasm-bindgen tool: the next native install step completed in one second.
